title: fragaria vesca subsp. monophylla
intro: Fragaria vesca subsp. monophylla, commonly known as the woodland strawberry, is a subspecies of strawberry native to Europe and Western Asia, characterized by having only one leaf at the tip of the petiole. This plant is valued for its potential health benefits, which include antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties that may aid in the prevention of diseases such as cardiovascular disease and certain types of cancer. The therapeutic actions of Fragaria vesca subsp. monophylla are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, phenolic acids, and ascorbic acid, which have been shown to exhibit antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-cancer activities. Additionally, the plant's leaves and fruits have been traditionally used in folk medicine to treat various health conditions, including fever, digestive issues, and respiratory problems.
